clue.text: Unexpected difficulty this, with two Xis causing absurd situation

definitions.text: Unexpected difficulty this, with two Xis causing absurd situation

parts.words: Unexpected difficulty this, with two Xis causing absurd situation
parts.note: a hidden snag is one sense; add the Roman numeral XXII (two lots of XI) and you get Heller's famous no-win bind

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a hitch that, doubled in Roman numerals, turns into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is Roman 11, so two XIs make XXII, 22; the answer followed by 22 is the title of Joseph Heller's novel and the phrase for a self-defeating absurd rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or hidden drawback is a common sense of the word, and with -22 added it names a paradoxical trap.

clue.text: Thought proof of existence lay in this philosophy

definitions.text: Thought proof of existence lay in this philosophy

parts.words: Thought proof of existence lay in this philosophy
parts.note: points to Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am', where thinking proves one exists

explanation.surface: A school of thought held that thinking proves you exist.
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes argued 'cogito ergo sum'; the system named after him uses his Latinised name Cartesius.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes' system is named after his Latin name, and his cogito made thought the proof of being.

clue.text: This rose in an Elizabethan house

explanation.surface: A rose growing at an Elizabethan mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: The heraldic rose of England's sixteenth-century dynasty, and Elizabeth I's royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VII's heraldic red-and-white rose bears this name, as does the dynasty that Elizabeth I belonged to.

clue.text: What one comes into, it appears, in her time of life

indicators.note: in says the little word goes inside the run of the other two

parts.note: age is one's time of life

explanation.surface: Something inherited, it seems, at her time of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it appears' looks like a comment on the clue but is padding; 'in' is the container signal, with the small word set inside the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: One comes into an inheritance, and a legacy handed down is the same idea.

clue.text: Sort of lobster that saw the end of Robespierre

definitions.text: that saw the end of Robespierre

explanation.surface: A seafood dish oddly credited with witnessing the downfall of a French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Robespierre fell in the coup of 9 Thermidor (July 1794), named for a month of the French Revolutionary calendar; the lobster dish was later named after a play of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobster in a creamy mustard sauce bears this name, and it was the revolutionary month of Robespierre's overthrow.

clue.text: Dangerous driver booked and pulled in, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word spoken that sounds like the entry

parts.note: a car pulled in by a truck is towed

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist is charged and his car hauled off.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is a notorious reckless motorist, 'booked' as he is in a book; 'pulled in' is towed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Grahame's motoring-mad amphibian is the dangerous driver found in a book.

clue.text: Additional art work for such a non-resident student

parts.note: extra means additional
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: Extra artwork is provided for a student living off campus.
explanation.walkthrough: An extramural student studies outside the university's walls; 'for such' makes the definition a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally outside the walls, the term covers courses taken by those not living at the university.

clue.text: In my circumstances unemployment pay is up in the air

indicators.note: in pairs with circumstances: the inner word is set in the surroundings of my
circumstances, things standing around, means my is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: is up means the dole is read from bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone out of work has their dole money uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reads the benefit backwards, as this is a down entry. 'up in the air' looks like uncertainty, but only 'air', a tune, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, the same as a melody.

clue.text: How to break a settlement in Latinised form

indicators.note: form here means a new shape for the letters of the word given

explanation.surface: A legal method expressed in Latin-flavoured wording.
explanation.walkthrough: To disentail is to free an estate from an entail, a legal settlement restricting who inherits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending an entail on property is breaking the legal settlement that fixed its inheritance.

clue.text: Capek's robots overcome a student of the country

indicators.note: overcome in a down entry puts the first piece on top of what follows

parts.note: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is Karel Capek's play that coined 'robot'
L is a learner

explanation.surface: Robots from a Czech play overpower a student from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside life is described by this adjective, the opposite of urban.

clue.text: Robin, the Bow Street runner

explanation.surface: A bird is equated with an officer of London's first police force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners, London's early police officers, wore red waistcoats and were nicknamed after the red-chested bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird's familiar name describes its red chest, and the same nickname was given to red-waistcoated Bow Street officers.

clue.text: Two notes returned to Lucy Locket for instance

indicators.note: returned means each of the two sol-fa syllables is read backwards

parts.note: sol (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme girl gets a couple of notes sent back to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SOL to LOS and RE to ER. In the nursery rhyme, Lucy Locket lost her pocket, so she is one who mislaid something.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme she lost her pocket, making her an example of someone who mislays things.

clue.text: Jack about to return with a list of corrections

indicators.note: to return asks for the pair of words before it to be read backwards as one run

parts.note: a jack, like a tar, is a sailor
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back carrying a list of mistakes to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns TAR + RE into ERRAT; then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed slip listing mistakes found in a book after printing goes by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Like numbers of clues for "prelate"

explanation.surface: Seems to compare numbers with the clues a setter might use for a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers one, two, three; and a setter cluing the word 'prelate' might well use this senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers are so called, and a senior Catholic churchman is a likely clue for a prelate.

clue.text: Luther as a professional writer when confronted by the devil

definitions.text: Luther as a professional writer when confronted by the devil

parts.words: Luther as a professional writer when confronted by the devil
parts.note: legend says Luther hurled his inkpot at the devil, so he literally threw ink; a hack journalist gets the same jokey name

explanation.surface: Martin Luther is cast as a jobbing author when facing Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: The story goes that Luther, at the Wartburg, threw an inkwell at the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack writer is jokingly called by the name that literally describes a thrower of ink.

clue.text: Native throws one soldier back into the river in Pakistan

indicators.note: into says the reversed run is thrown inside the river's name

parts.note: the Indus is Pakistan's main river

indicators.note: back means the words one and soldier are read in reverse as a single run

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A local hurls a soldier backwards into a Pakistani river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the soldier phrase as one run, and 'into' sets that inside the river; 'throws' only serves the picture of hurling someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and indigenous both describe something originating in a particular place.

clue.text: Said yes very quietly to remedy for indigestion

indicators.note: to remedy means to put right, so the letters are reset

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, means very quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone murmured agreement to a cure for a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remedy' rearranges SAIDYES with PP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical name for an upset stomach after eating.

clue.text: A little elephant in one's stocking?

explanation.surface: Asks whether a baby elephant might turn up in a Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: A young elephant is so called, and the same word is the fleshy back of the lower leg, which is inside one's stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Young elephants, like young cattle, bear this name, and it is also the back of the lower leg that a stocking covers.

clue.text: Once a mercenary sort of writer perhaps

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune of old, or some kind of author.
explanation.walkthrough: In medieval times a free lance was a knight who sold his services; now the word describes self-employed writers and others.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval knights for hire went by this name, and today a self-employed journalist does too.

clue.text: Wakefield vicar in Disraeli's league

explanation.surface: A clergyman from Wakefield joins a political society.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Primrose is Goldsmith's Vicar of Wakefield; the Primrose League was a Conservative organisation founded in memory of Disraeli, whose favourite flower it was.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith's clergyman bears this name, as does the Tory league honouring Disraeli's favourite flower.

clue.text: The Dong's leading feature

parts.note: Edward Lear's Dong with a Luminous one: the part that leads, being out in front of his face

explanation.surface: The most prominent trait of a nonsense character.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's poem The Dong with a Luminous Nose; 'leading' works both as chief and as literally out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's creature is famed for its glowing facial protrusion, the bit of anyone that goes first.

clue.text: What's on foot? Paranormal perception — a standard procedure, note

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception
a drill is a set routine
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A list of psychic powers, routines and a note, oddly answering what one wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope-soled canvas shoe is something worn on the foot.

clue.text: Unveiled the work of Richard Strauss

definitions.text: Unveiled the work of Richard Strauss

parts.words: Unveiled the work of Richard Strauss
parts.note: the Strauss opera whose heroine sheds seven veils in her dance

explanation.surface: A premiere of a Strauss opera is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera's famous Dance of the Seven Veils has the title character remove veils one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss's 1905 opera about Herod's stepdaughter features the Dance of the Seven Veils.

clue.text: I heard about the age of musical drama

indicators.note: about means the word for eye-related goes around the age

parts.note: I said aloud is eye, and optic means relating to the eye
an era is an age

explanation.surface: Someone says they have heard about the period of musical theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I heard' is 'eye' said aloud, and the eye's adjective is the outer piece; 'about' wraps it round the age.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is musical drama, and this adjective means belonging to it.

clue.text: "As false as dicers' -—"(Hamlet)

parts.note: complete Hamlet's line to Gertrude about marriage vows: gamblers' solemn promises

explanation.surface: Hamlet's line likening broken vows to gamblers' promises, with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet tells his mother her act makes marriage vows as false as gamblers' sworn promises (Act 3, Scene 4).
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn promises sworn by gamblers were proverbially worthless, which is Hamlet's point about vows.

clue.text: Having no principles, gives morning test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An unprincipled person sets a test in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any moral sense is what it means to be without principles.

clue.text: Unlimited speech shows scale of representation

indicators.note: unlimited means without limits, so the first and last letters of the formal address go

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Free speech reveals a scale of representation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' removes the first and last letters of ORATION, leaving RATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A map's scale is expressed as a proportion of map distance to real distance.

clue.text: Was aware of 19, say, in the past

definitions.text: Was aware of 19, say, in the past

parts.words: Was aware of 19, say, in the past
parts.note: the entry at 19, the facial feature, sounds like the present tense for being aware; put that verb into the past

explanation.surface: Someone was conscious of something earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 19-across is NOSE, which sounds like 'knows'; in the past tense 'knows' becomes this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware in the past is the past tense of know.

clue.text: News agency has nothing on the poet

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A news agency has nothing on a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance poet of Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato is the sixteenth-century Italian writer of epic verse.

clue.text: Arm with material that's explosive

definitions.note: explosive is used as a noun here, an explosive substance

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
cotton is a fabric

explanation.surface: Equip yourself with something that's liable to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrocellulose, made by treating fibres with nitric acid, is a blasting substance.

clue.text: No Beau Brummell involved in soccer war

indicators.note: involved here means tangled up, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A dandy is not to be found mixed up in a football war.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Brummell was the famous Regency dandy, so 'No Beau Brummell' is a scruffily dressed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A field figure in old rags is the opposite of the elegant Regency dandy.

clue.text: Call up the day before receiving authorization

indicators.note: receiving means the eve takes the approval inside it

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival
OK is approval or authorization

explanation.surface: Ring someone up the day before getting permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon up a memory or feeling is to call it to mind.
